Hi,

the data argument to inla.stack needs something different, eg.

    data = list(pa = dam$pa)

if your model formula is
  pa ~ ...

Finn

On Thu, 17 Sep 2020 at 03:04, Yuki Kanamori <y.kan...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi, 

I have a trouble in inla.stack() when I analyze presence/absence data.
The model I want to fit is the same as the example using SPDEtoy data, but I have a error; error in l[[k]] <- rep(l[[k]], n.A).
(I confirmed that the example using SPDEtoy run successfully.)

I do not know where is mistake in my code and how to resolve the error.
A dammy data is attached and my code is below.


# data ----------------------------------------------------------
setwd()
dam = read.csv("dam.csv")
lonlat = cbind(dam$lng, dam$lat)


# create mesh ---------------------------------------------------
dom = cbind(c(139.7, 139.5, 139.7, 140.1, 140.3, 139.9), # x-axis 
                c(35.2,  35.4,  35.8,  35.8,  35.4,  35.2))

mesh = inla.mesh.2d(loc.domain = dom, lonlat, max.edge = c(1, 1), cutoff = 0.5, offset = c(0.3, 0.2))

spde = inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh = mesh, alpha = 2, prior.range = c(0.01, 0.05), prior.sigma = c(1, 0.01))

A_dam = inla.spde.make.A(mesh, loc = lonlat)

# check
dim(A_dam) #199, 35
table(rowSums(A_dam > 0))
table(rowSums(A_dam))
table(colSums(A_dam) > 0)
table(as.numeric(A_dam))


# stack ---------------------------------------------------------
stack_obs = inla.stack(
  data = dam$pa,
  A = list(A_dam, 1),
  effects = list(i = 1:spde$n.spde,
                 intercept = rep(1, nrow(dam)),
  tag = "obs"
)


Best regards,
Yuki Kanamori
